---
title: "Does a person's shift repeat?"
subtitle: "One luteal − follicular vector per closed cycle, 17 features. Interval 2022, 24 participants with two or three cycles."
---

Not detectably. The mean distance between one person's own cycle vectors equals the mean distance to other people's: ratio **1.00 [0.92, 1.08]** over 17 features, 0.97 [0.84, 1.10] over the six device signals. Per feature, resting heart rate is the one signal with a repeatable personal shift (ICC 0.61 [0.09, 0.86]). The wrist-temperature rise, the cohort's most reliable, does not repeat within a person at this sampling density (ICC −0.02 [−0.34, 0.31]).

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[42 participants<br/>3,698 labelled days] --> B[87 closed cycles<br/>from menstrual onsets]
    B --> C[66 cycles with ≥ 3 days<br/>in both phases, 39 participants]
    C --> D[24 participants with ≥ 2 such cycles<br/>51 cycles, at most 3 each]
    D --> E[within 4.20 vs between 4.21<br/>ratio 1.00, 0.92 to 1.08]
```

![A: mean Euclidean distance between a person's own cycle vectors and between her cycles and other people's, 95 % BCa over 5,000 participant resamples. B: ICC(1) of each feature's shift across a person's cycles. Filled: device signals.](figures/F2_repeatability.png)

## The numbers

| Quantity | 17 features | 6 device signals |
|---|---|---|
| Participants with ≥ 2 eligible closed cycles | 24 (51 cycles) | 22 (46 cycles) |
| Mean within-person distance | 4.20 [3.73, 4.79] | 2.03 [1.67, 2.61] |
| Mean between-person distance, same participants | 4.21 [3.88, 4.55] | 2.09 [1.82, 2.43] |
| **Ratio within / between** | **1.00 [0.92, 1.08]** | **0.97 [0.84, 1.10]** |
| Between-person variance component, summed over features | 0 at the point estimate | 0.03 [0, 0.64] |
| Cycles at which personal data would beat the cohort mean | not estimable | not estimable |

Distances are in pooled between-person SD units summed over the features, so the two columns are not comparable with each other.

## Read with

- **Two or three cycles per person, 24 people.** An ICC from pairs has large sampling error; the ratio's interval spans 0.92 to 1.08. This is what one three-month interval can show, not a statement about physiology.
- **Day-to-day noise attenuates every ICC.** On synthetic data with a planted repeatability of 0.8, this estimator returned 0.36 to 0.56.
- **The scale compresses the device signals.** Distances use the between-person spread of phase means as their unit, so a consistent 3 bpm shift against baselines that differ by 7 bpm between people counts for less than a one-point symptom shift. With 17 equal-weight features, symptom noise dominates the vector.
- **Resting heart rate reaches 14 participants** because a cycle needs three valid days in each phase and 782 of 3,698 days were coded 0.
- A negative ICC means two cycles of the same person differ more than two cycles of different people. With these intervals, stress and sleep issues are observations to carry, not findings.

## Next

A variance-component analysis of the five device signals that separates day-to-day noise from cycle-to-cycle and person-to-person variation, on the spread of the shifts themselves, with the number of cycles a person needs before her own data outweigh the cohort shift. Built and tested on synthetic data; the real run is pending.

Tables: [`tables/feature_icc.csv`](tables/feature_icc.csv), [`tables/repeatability_summary.json`](tables/repeatability_summary.json). The between-person variance component was zero at the point estimate, so the crossing number of cycles is not estimable and is not in the file.
